texts.preamble: The Corporation Of The City Of Nagpur vs Vilas Dadaraoji Deshmukh And ... on 29 July, 2019 Author: V. M. Deshpande Bench: V. M. Deshpande Judg.Cril.apeal55- 1/6 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Nagpur Bench, Nagpur. Criminal Appeal No. 55 Of 2005 The Corporation of the City of Nagpur, Through its Food Inspector, Shri S. J. Rajurkar .. Appellant ...Versus...
texts.facts: By the present appeal, the appellant is challenging the judgment and order of acquittal passed by NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nagpur in Regular Criminal Case No. 13/1993. From 1985 till his retirement he was working as Food Inspector in Nagpur Municipal Corporation. 6] On 01/12/1992, he paid a visit to New M.L.A. Canteen, Nagpur along with Panch-Rajesh Sabale, who was not examined during the trial. At that time, deceased respondent-Vilas Deshmukh was present. Shri Shrikrushna Rajankar gave his identification and inspected the canteen. He prepared inspection report and gave a copy to Shri Vilas Deshmukh. The copy of the report is at Exh. 30. 7] During inspection, he found one open chilly powder bag containing about 5 Kg. without label. On inquiry deceased Vilas Deshmukh disclosed that the said chilly powder is used for preparing eatables and other food articles. Complainant disclosed his intention to deceased accused and obtained sample of said chilly powder. Six Hundred grams of chilly powder was taken. It was put in a pot. Rupees twenty seven was paid towards price of the said chilly powder. The NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt receipt was executed, it is at Exh. 31. 8] Thereafter, complainant prepared three copies of Form No.VI. One was given to the accused/deceased. Office copy of Form No.VI is at Exh. 32. Thereafter, the complainant prepared three copies of the notice under Section 14-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Original was given to deceased Vilas Deshmukh and the office copy having his signature is at Exh.33. 9] Complainant divided 600 grams of chilly powder in three equal parts and taken in three glass bottles and put lead on each glass bottle. Thereafter, seal was prepared. Thereafter, he returned to the office and under the sealed condition the articles were sent to the Public Analyst, Regional Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur. On 06/01/1993 complainant received report from Public Analyst, Regional Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur. Report is at Exh. 43. It does not show that the chilly powder was confirming standard. Thereafter, following other usual steps the complaint was filed. It would be relevant to reproduce herein paragraph 21 from the evidence of complainant and it is reproduced herein: The Corporation Of The City Of Nagpur vs Vilas Dadaraoji Deshmukh And ... on 29 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126401985/ I did not record the statement of accused no.2. I took sample bottles from Store of Health Dept. prior to four or five days on 1/12/1992. The sample bottles were not sterilized. I have not fasten the entire thread by sealing wax, on the paper cover."
texts.arguments: 11] In view of the admission as given by the complainant, the learned counsel for the appellant fairly states that the mandatory provisions of Rule 16 and 14 were not properly followed by the complainant. The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate in my view has not NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt committed any mistake while acquitting the accused persons, especially when the mandatory provisions of sealing and taking the sample in a dry clean jar were not followed.
